title: Dioscin attenuates D‑galactose‑induced retinal pigment epithelium senescence and epithelial-mesenchymal transition via the TGF‑beta2/PI3K/Akt/beta‑catenin pathway.
authors: Ouyang, Qi; Zhou, Huiqin; Ji, Chenhao; Jiang, Hong; Zhao, Linhui; Pan, Yiwei; Xiang, Shuanglin; Hu, Xiang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物Dioscin通过TGF-beta2/PI3K/Akt/beta-catenin通路缓解RPE衰老与EMT，虽含分子对接但核心为细胞/动物实验，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of Dioscin in an age-related macular degeneration (AMD) -like model and to explore its potential therapeutic mechanisms. METHODS: The therapeutic potential of Dioscin for AMD was investigated using D-galactose-induced senescence models in ARPE-19 cells (an in vitro preliminary screening model) and C57BL/6J mice using RT-qPCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence, and SA-beta-gal staining. Bioinformatic analysis and molecular docking identified TGF-beta2 as a computationally predicted potential target of Dioscin in AMD. Key mechanisms involving TGF-beta2 and the PI3K/Akt/beta-catenin signaling pathway were assessed in vitro using RT-qPCR, western blotting. RESULTS: In D-galactose-induced senescence models, Dioscin significantly alleviated RPE senescence and EMT. Single-cell transcriptome analysis revealed that TGF-beta2 is highly expressed in choroidal vascular endothelial cells of AMD patients. Mechanistically, computational predictions (molecular docking and dynamics simulations) identified TGF-beta2 as a computationally predicted potential target of Dioscin, and experimental data showed that Dioscin suppressed D-galactose-induced activation of the TGF-beta2/PI3K/Akt/beta-catenin pathway in RPE cells, suggesting a potential paracrine regulatory mechanism. CONCLUSION: Dioscin alleviates RPE senescence and EMT through suppression of the TGF-beta2/PI3K/Akt/beta-catenin pathway. Single-cell transcriptomics reveals that TGF-beta2 is specifically upregulated in choroidal vascular endothelial cells in AMD, suggesting a paracrine mechanism linking vascular pathology to RPE dysfunction. These findings suggest that Dioscin may have potential value in mitigating RPE senescence and EMT in an AMD‑like model, although further validation in more clinically relevant AMD models is required.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在评估薯蓣皂苷（Dioscin）在年龄相关性黄斑变性（age-related macular degeneration, AMD）样模型中的保护作用，并探讨其潜在治疗机制。方法：采用D-半乳糖诱导的ARPE-19细胞衰老模型（体外初步筛选模型）和C57BL/6J小鼠模型，通过RT-qPCR、western blotting、免疫荧光和SA-β-半乳糖苷酶染色，研究Dioscin对AMD的治疗潜力。生物信息学分析和分子对接将TGF-β2确定为Dioscin在AMD中经计算预测的潜在靶点。在体外，使用RT-qPCR和western blotting评估涉及TGF-β2及PI3K/Akt/β-catenin信号通路的关键机制。结果：在D-半乳糖诱导的衰老模型中，Dioscin显著缓解了视网膜色素上皮（RPE）衰老和上皮-间质转化（EMT）。单细胞转录组分析显示，TGF-β2在AMD患者的脉络膜血管内皮细胞中高表达。机制上，计算预测（分子对接和动力学模拟）将TGF-β2确定为Dioscin的潜在靶点，实验数据表明，Dioscin抑制了D-半乳糖诱导的RPE细胞中TGF-β2/PI3K/Akt/β-catenin通路激活，提示存在潜在的旁分泌调控机制。结论：Dioscin通过抑制TGF-β2/PI3K/Akt/β-catenin通路缓解RPE衰老和EMT。单细胞转录组学揭示，TGF-β2在AMD的脉络膜血管内皮细胞中特异性上调，提示血管病理与RPE功能障碍之间存在旁分泌机制关联。这些发现表明，Dioscin在AMD样模型中可能具有缓解RPE衰老和EMT的潜在价值，但需在更具临床相关性的AMD模型中进一步验证。
